title: Piercing Statue Solo #150 (힙컷 · P25 집중형 · 몸통 3조각 · 왼팔 투명(에메랄드 그린 유리) · 오른팔 목재(purpleheart) · 몸통 [대각 3조각(좌상→우하)] 투명(자수정) / 내용물(코발트 블루 유리+나비) / 목재(wenge) · 왼허벅지 수조(내용물 물) · 오른허벅지 내용물(코발트 블루 유리+수정 조각) · 체형 giant hourglass frame flaring · 쉬농 · 비비드블루 · 메이크업 반바 · 금속 황동 · 쥬얼리 헤어 장식·목걸이 JQ5)
prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, hip-cut statue multi-material portrait: real face and neck, and a sculpted body made of different materials — her left arm clear crystal, her right arm carved wood, her torso split into three pieces (clear crystal, solid glass holding embedded objects and carved wood), her left thigh a glass vessel full of water and her right thigh solid glass holding embedded objects. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to two individually rounded, deliberately carved tips a short way down her thighs, just below the hip line, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her sculpted form comes to an end at her thighs, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Japanese woman — a deep bronze tan foundation over real skin, thick white paint bands above and below both eyes lying on the lids and never across the eyeballs, neon pink and lime paint strokes across the cheekbones, rhinestone and star stickers clustered on the cheeks and forehead only, long false lashes, large eyes with bright real catchlights, glossy white lips, a fierce, playful expression, bold vivid electric-blue hair styled in a low chignon knot at the nape. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. Her neck, the hollows above her collarbones and the tops of her shoulders carry the same real living skin as her face: visible pores and fine skin grain, a soft sheen of natural skin oils on the highest planes, faint fine peach-fuzz hairs catching the rim light, gentle tonal variation with a natural warm flush, and the fine natural creases of a real neck — never airbrushed, never smooth like plastic. Like any real person she is slightly asymmetrical: a few small natural beauty marks and freckles scattered unevenly, one side of her neck and shoulder very slightly warmer and more freckled than the other.

Piercings: All twenty-five piercings gather mostly on the left side of her face, and the right side stays almost bare: on the left ear eight oversized pieces — a huge antique-brass hoop hanging clear of the neck down to the shoulder, a wide antique-brass ear cuff, three smaller antique-brass rings, two thick antique-brass bars and a small antique-brass stud up to the top; one small antique-brass stud sits in the right ear; four antique-brass pieces in a row along the outer half of the left eyebrow, alternating small rings that pass through the brow skin with the skin visible through each loop and small round ball studs sitting on the skin; two small antique-brass rings pass through the left nostril and a thick antique-brass septum ring hangs below the nose; a antique-brass hoop passes through the left edge of the lower lip with a antique-brass snake-bite ring beside it and a small antique-brass ring at the left edge of the upper lip; a antique-brass Medusa stud sits above the lips; a antique-brass labret stud and a small antique-brass ring sit on the chin; three small antique-brass studs run along the left jaw. Each piece carries small rubies set into the metal. All jewelry is real antique brass, sitting in real, calm, healthy skin — no redness, no swelling, no irritation — with a small natural warm shadow under each piece. Every piece stays at least a finger's width from the eyeballs, and no chain or bar crosses the eyes.

Piercing depth: every bar and surface bar is embedded in the skin — its middle runs beneath the skin so only its two end studs show on the surface, the skin between them faintly raised over the hidden bar, with a small warm shadow at each end and nothing lying on top of the skin like a sticker. Every ring passes through a small healed opening in the skin, the skin visible through the loop, and every stud sits through the skin with its back hidden. Where a bar, ring or stud goes through the ear, the lip, the nostril or the brow, it passes through the real tissue with the skin wrapping snugly around it.

Jewelry: besides the piercings she wears well over ten pieces, an extreme maximalist stack of platinum hair ornaments set in her hair; well over ten pieces, an extreme maximalist stack of platinum necklaces and chains resting on her neck, collarbones and upper chest, all of it real, sitting on and over the material of her body and her real neck and hair without covering her eyes, her face or her piercings.

Physique: A giant hourglass frame flaring at both ends — broad shoulders, a colossal chest projecting past them, a big round belly, hips as broad as the shoulders, both thighs clearly separate and individually shaped, her left arm clear crystal, her right arm carved wood, her torso split into three pieces (clear crystal, solid glass holding embedded objects and carved wood), her left thigh a glass vessel full of water and her right thigh solid glass holding embedded objects.

Boundary (skin to material, at underarm height): A single straight, horizontal line runs across her body at underarm height, level with both armpits. Real skin above this line — her face, neck, both shoulders, and the very tops of both upper arms. Below this line, completely different materials meet at her body's natural joints (both shoulders, both hips) and at the seams inside the torso, each keeping its own distinct appearance right up to where it touches its neighbour, never blending into it. At the underarm line itself, the material immediately below rises in a small raised step above her skin, casting a crisp shadow. Shards interlock along this line only.

Left arm (shoulder to hand): solid transparent material, solid clear emerald-green cast glass, with slow internal swirls and tiny bubbles, deep bottle-green where thickest and pale lime at every thin edge, one continuous carved mass, never hollow, every wrist, palm, finger and knuckle the same material. Light passes straight through it; the backdrop is visibly bent inside it.

Right arm (shoulder to hand): carved from ONE solid block of deep violet purpleheart wood, a dense hardwood of rich purple with fine straight grain, polished to a hard satin sheen, completely opaque, completely opaque, every wrist, palm, finger and knuckle the same wood, the grain running unbroken through it. No light passes through it — only reflections on its polished surface.

Torso (underarm line down to where the thighs begin): The torso, from the underarm line down to where the thighs begin, is divided into 3 diagonal pieces by 2 parallel straight diagonal seams running from the upper left to the lower right as seen by the camera, crossing the centre line of the torso about 36% and 66% of the way down it. Torso piece 1 (the piece above the first diagonal seam): solid transparent material, solid amethyst crystal, with internal facets and colour zoning, deep violet where thickest and pale lilac at every thin edge, one continuous carved mass, never hollow. Light passes straight through it; the backdrop is visibly bent inside it. Torso piece 2 (the diagonal band between the two seams): carved from ONE solid block of deep cobalt-blue cast glass, with slow internal swirls and tiny bubbles, near-navy where thickest and bright cobalt at every thin edge, never hollow, never split; suspended deep within it, visible through it like objects frozen inside a single flawless crystal, are a dozen small, perfectly carved crystal butterflies with delicate translucent wings, each one a paler, brighter facet than the crystal around it, each one fully embedded in the solid material with no cavity and no liquid around it. Light passes through the solid material; the backdrop is visibly bent inside it. Torso piece 3 (the piece below the second diagonal seam, reaching the bottom of the torso): carved from ONE solid block of dark wenge wood, a deep near-black wood finely striped with narrow gold-tan pinstripes running through it, polished to a hard satin sheen, completely opaque, completely opaque, the grain running unbroken through it. No light passes through it — only reflections on its polished surface.

Left thigh (hip down to its tip, a short way down her thighs, just below the hip line): a sculpted vessel of the same clear glass (unmistakably glass: thick, crystal-clear and polished, bright specular reflections, sharp white highlights, tiny trapped bubbles), completely filled to the brim with clear water holding a few white lily blossoms floating slowly inside it, never crowding, mostly open clear water around each one. It curves inward and seals shut into its own smooth, rounded, closed tip, the water continuing unbroken down to that tip. Light passes through; the backdrop is visibly bent inside it.

Right thigh (hip down to its tip, a short way down her thighs, just below the hip line): carved from ONE solid block of deep cobalt-blue cast glass, with slow internal swirls and tiny bubbles, near-navy where thickest and bright cobalt at every thin edge, never hollow, never split; suspended deep within it, visible through it like objects frozen inside a single flawless crystal, are dozens of small, jagged clear quartz shards like frozen lightning bolts, each one a brighter, sharper facet than the glass around it, each one fully embedded in the solid material with no cavity and no liquid around it. Light passes through the solid material; the backdrop is visibly bent inside it. The right thigh ends in its own smooth, deeply polished rounded tip, finished the way a carved sculpture is finished.

Where each material meets its neighbour (left shoulder, right shoulder, left hip, right hip, and every seam inside the torso), the two distinct materials sit flush against each other with a thin, clean seam, deliberate and precise, never jagged, torn or blended — always the finish of a sculpture, each material keeping its own colour, clarity and surface completely separate from the one beside it. Both thighs stay clearly separate all the way down, never merging into a single base, both rounded tips resting side by side on the surface beneath her.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a warm golden amber on one side and a bright citrus yellow on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle — glowing evenly, marked with a few thin dark vertical lines so the bending of those lines is visible wherever the body is transparent, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, body angled 45 degrees, her left hand resting on her flared hip, her right arm held clear of her body with the hand relaxed at hip height, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: two large softboxes rake across her body from either side, so a warm golden amber light glances off the left half and a bright citrus yellow light glances off the right half — passing straight through the transparent parts (left arm, left thigh, right thigh, torso piece 1, torso piece 2), while only reflecting off the opaque parts (right arm, torso piece 3). A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears. Shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
